verdict.rationale: Viam documents official SDKs across Python, Go, C++, TypeScript and Flutter. Its machine and fleet APIs are callable from those SDKs, and the SDKs handle transport, sessions and auto-reconnect. The docs explicitly position SDKs as the way an AI agent can operate a machine, and the GitHub repo confirms multiple client SDKs. Missing for 10: per-language SDK reference/package detail in evidence, hands-on independent corroboration of SDK quality.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Write your control logic in Python or Go, get lower-level control with C++, or build a client application with Typescript or Flutter.
Multiple SDKs are available for writing client applications that interface with the Viam RDK.
The machine API allows you to connect to your machine from within a supported Viam SDK, retrieve status information, and send commands remotely.
They open the transport (WebRTC where appropriate, gRPC otherwise), manage sessions for safety, and reconnect automatically when the network drops.
An AI agent with a shell or an SDK can operate a Viam machine the same way a person or a program can.
